sentences.en: We live in this world where like one in 10,000 airplanes could fall out of a sky and it's okay.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在这样一个世界里，万分之一的飞机可能会坠毁，但这没关系。

sentences.en: That's software development for you.
sentences.zh: 这就是软件开发。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, and that's the reality of, of software too, is, is there are problems all the time that you do not anticipate.
sentences.zh: 这就是软件的现实，总会有你预料不到的问题。

sentences.en: You cannot anticipate, but you have to try, you always have to be defensive in your programming to your point earlier.
sentences.zh: 你无法预料，但你必须尝试，正如你之前所说，编程时必须时刻保持防御性。

sentences.en: Like we add this logging in here just in case this weird scenario happens or something is null that we didn't expect to be null, but you have to account for it because if it can
sentences.zh: 比如我们添加这些日志，以防出现奇怪的情况，或者某个本不该为空的东西变为空了，你必须考虑到这一点，因为如果它可能

sentences.en: be, it will happen.
sentences.zh: 发生，它就一定会发生。

sentences.en: It happens every time.
sentences.zh: 每次都会发生。

sentences.en: You had to give a firsthand example.
sentences.zh: 你得举个亲身经历的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we rolled out, uh, I rolled out the eternal terminal, which is this SSH, uh, uh, uh, alternative.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们推出了 Eternal Terminal，这是 SSH 的一个替代品。

sentences.en: And, uh, one thing I didn't expect was, was people running out of memory because, uh, you know, I'm looking at my desktop here as 64 gigs of Ram.
sentences.zh: 我没预料到的一件事是人们会耗尽内存，因为我看着我的桌面有 64G 内存。

sentences.en: My laptop has probably the same.
sentences.zh: 我的笔记本电脑可能也一样。

sentences.en: And, uh, it's just, I didn't really think about, you know, eternal terminal uses maybe 50 megs.
sentences.zh: 我真的没考虑到 Eternal Terminal 可能只用 50MB 内存。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But, but someone out there was running it on a VM that they got for free.
sentences.zh: 但有人在免费获得的虚拟机上运行它。

sentences.en: And, uh, and, uh, yeah, just all, all things started, uh, breaking all over the place.
sentences.zh: 然后，所有东西都开始到处崩溃。

sentences.en: And it's because every time you ask for memory, you could end up not getting it.
sentences.zh: 这是因为每次你申请内存时，最终都可能申请不到。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, it's just, that stuff ends up being really difficult to do after the fact, you know, and, and you're, uh, adding to that topic,
sentences.zh: 嗯，事后处理这些问题确实非常困难，而且补充一点，

sentences.en: we never think about performance these days because computers are fast and we have fast internet, right.
sentences.zh: 我们现在从不考虑性能，因为电脑很快，互联网也很快，对吧。

sentences.en: But, but what happens when you're working on an airplane that's flying over the Pacific ocean that has the worst wifi connection in the entire world?
sentences.zh: 但当你在一架飞越太平洋的飞机上，连接着世界上最烂的 Wi-Fi 时会发生什么？

sentences.en: And you're trying to use a website, right?
sentences.zh: 你试图使用一个网站，对吧？

sentences.en: You're trying to surf the web or do something.
sentences.zh: 你试图上网或做点什么。

sentences.en: And it's in, it's like the slowest thing in the world, but as developers, we don't think about those scenarios.
sentences.zh: 它慢得要命，但作为开发人员，我们从不考虑这些场景。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's, it's all those sorts of scenarios that we never think about that then cause all sorts of errors and bad user experience.
sentences.zh: 正是所有这些我们从未考虑过的场景，导致了各种错误和糟糕的用户体验。

sentences.en: But yeah.
sentences.zh: 但确实。

sentences.en: And that's where I think, uh, you know, tools like, like stackify really important because they give you a window into the entire user base.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为像 Stackify 这样的工具非常重要的原因，因为它们让你能洞察整个用户群。

sentences.en: And there is that, that needle in the haystack, which we talked about earlier.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们之前谈到的，大海捞针。

sentences.en: And, and, uh, that seems pretty overwhelming, but, but with the right tools and the right, uh, you know, the right logging, you can actually find that person who maybe
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，这看起来确实让人不知所措，但只要有合适的工具和，呃，你知道，合适的日志记录，你实际上可以找到那个人，也许

sentences.en: right now is flying over the Pacific using your app.
sentences.zh: 此刻正用着你的应用飞越太平洋。

sentences.en: Well, you mentioned, and you mentioned your logging, um, logging is really important, but it's, it's even more important to do the right type of logging and using logging levels.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你提到了，你提到了你的日志记录，嗯，日志记录确实非常重要，但更重要的是采用正确的日志记录方式并使用日志级别。

sentences.en: So it's like, you know, that weird scenario you mentioned that needs to be logged at like a warning or error or fatal level, right?
sentences.zh: 所以就像你提到的那种奇怪的情况，需要记录为警告、错误或致命级别，对吧？

sentences.en: Not a debug level, you know, and, and that's, and that's where when people, people's apps get deployed to production, a lot
sentences.zh: 而不是调试级别，你知道，这就是为什么当人们的应用部署到生产环境时，很多

sentences.en: of times debug logs and stuff aren't turned on because they can be like a crazy volume of
sentences.zh: 时候调试日志之类的东西没有开启，因为它们可能会产生海量的

sentences.en: information, but you need to look for things that are warnings or error or fatal and those types of severity.
sentences.zh: 信息，但你需要关注的是那些警告、错误或致命等严重级别的信息。

sentences.en: Um, and, and then it makes it easy to log into a tool like Stackfile and say, okay,
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后这使得登录像 Stackify 这样的工具变得很容易，你可以说，好吧，

sentences.en: let's look at all the logs that are warning or fatal or whatever, um, and go find those probleMs.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看所有警告或致命之类的日志，嗯，然后去找出那些问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, that totally makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，这完全说得通。

sentences.en: What about, um, how do you handle machines that are misbehaving?
sentences.zh: 那么，嗯，你是如何处理那些运行异常的机器的呢？

sentences.en: So, so in this case, you know, if you look at the overall data, it might be fine, but you, I had,
sentences.zh: 所以，在这种情况下，你知道，如果你看整体数据，可能没问题，但我，我记得，

sentences.en: I remember an issue, um, that we had a number of years ago where, um, basically our app was creating new threads.
sentences.zh: 我记得几年前我们遇到的一个问题，嗯，基本上我们的应用在不断创建新线程。

sentences.en: And so it was just constantly creating new threads.
sentences.zh: 它就是一直在创建新线程。

sentences.en: And at some point, uh, the machine would die and, uh, you know, AWS or whatever the cloud we're using
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，呃，机器会崩溃，呃，你知道，AWS 或者我们使用的任何云服务

sentences.en: would just kill that machine, um, based on some logic they had, uh, and then it would spin another one up.
sentences.zh: 会根据它们的一些逻辑直接杀掉那台机器，嗯，然后它会再启动一台新的。

sentences.en: And so it's one of these things that we actually, it took us a long time to even know something was wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以这是那种我们花了很长时间才意识到出问题的事情之一。

sentences.en: Um, because you can't, you can't really tell, but if you were to look at a single machine, you could see that things were getting kind of bad, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为你真的看不出来，但如果你观察单台机器，你就能看出情况正在变糟，对吧？

sentences.en: And so how do you handle that?
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何处理这种情况的呢？

sentences.en: We have this sort of heterogeneous environment where some machines are healthy, some aren't.
sentences.zh: 我们有这种异构环境，有些机器健康，有些则不然。

sentences.en: So I had this exact type of issue happen this week at Stackify.
sentences.zh: 这周在 Stackify 我就遇到了完全一样的问题。

sentences.en: We deployed a new application on Kubernetes in our QA environment.
sentences.zh: 我们在 QA 环境的 Kubernetes 上部署了一个新应用。

sentences.en: And for whatever reason, the, the, the pod would fail and then Kubernetes would restart the pod and create a new one.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，那个 Pod 会失败，然后 Kubernetes 会重启 Pod 并创建一个新的。

sentences.en: Except the problem is, is it did it 7,000 times over like three days.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，它在三天内重复了 7000 次。

sentences.en: And then Kubernetes ran out of memory.
sentences.zh: 然后 Kubernetes 内存耗尽了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: The, the, the, the node and the cluster like ran out of memory.
sentences.zh: 那个节点和集群内存耗尽了。

sentences.en: Now, luckily this was in QA and it wasn't a big deal, but these things happen to your point, like things that you don't anticipate.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是这发生在 QA 环境，没什么大不了的，但正如你所说，这些事情会发生，有些是你无法预料的。

sentences.en: And, and actually the fix for that was we had just put memory limits on the pod and then it behaved just fine.
sentences.zh: 实际上解决办法就是我们给 Pod 设置了内存限制，然后它就运行正常了。

sentences.en: Like just really weird stuff.
sentences.zh: 就是些非常奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: And to, to your point, like these are problems that, that still happen.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这些问题依然会发生。

sentences.en: Um, we've got another app in
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在

sentences.en: Stackify that's, that's, uh, actually in production for us.
sentences.zh: Stackify 还有另一个应用，实际上是在生产环境中运行的。

sentences.en: And the only way we can make the thing work is to restart it every 30 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们让它正常工作的唯一方法就是每 30 分钟重启一次。

sentences.en: Oh no, that's so brutal.
sentences.zh: 哦不，那太残酷了。

sentences.en: And, but these things happen, right?
sentences.zh: 但这些事情就是会发生，对吧？

sentences.en: And you're like, okay, do we spend like millions of man hours and dollars fixing this thing?
sentences.zh: 你会想，好吧，我们要花数百万的人工时和美元去修复这个东西吗？

sentences.en: Or do we make a script to restart it every 30 minutes?
sentences.zh: 还是写个脚本每 30 分钟重启一次？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That is, that is a really good point, right?
sentences.zh: 那确实是一个很好的观点，对吧？

sentences.en: Is it's, you know, especially when we dive into this, it's easy to kind of say, well, we'll log everything.
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道，特别是在我们深入研究时，很容易说，好吧，我们会记录一切。

sentences.en: Uh, you know, we'll, we will do a deployment once a year or something like that, but, but there's always these, uh, trade-offs, right?
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道，我们会一年部署一次之类的，但总是存在这些，呃，权衡，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, you know, it could be that if your business doesn't move fast enough, like if you're
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你的业务发展不够快，比如如果你

sentences.en: not pivoting, uh, based on the user experience fast enough, um, that, that you fail at the business level.
sentences.zh: 没有根据用户体验快速调整，嗯，那么你在业务层面就会失败。

sentences.en: And so you're kind of running up against that.
sentences.zh: 所以你有点在面对这个问题。

sentences.en: You have to kind of balance.
sentences.zh: 你必须进行某种平衡。

sentences.en: And this is one of the things that, um, that I think a good tech lead will, will do well is balance sort of moving fast
sentences.zh: 我认为一个优秀的技术主管会做好的事情之一，就是平衡快速推进

sentences.en: or, or maybe being sort of more interactive with the other cross-functional teams, balance that against, you know, accumulating all this technical debt.
sentences.zh: 或者说与跨职能团队进行更多互动，与积累所有这些技术债务进行权衡。

sentences.en: And so I think that's, that's like requires constant supervision.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这需要持续的监督。

sentences.en: Well, and we could record a whole podcast episode just on this topic, but the, the problem is software developers always chase shiny objects, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们可以专门录一期播客来讨论这个话题，但问题是软件开发者总是追逐闪亮的新事物，对吧？

sentences.en: They're like,
sentences.zh: 他们会说，

sentences.en: Hey, we want to rewrite everything in Kubernetes because why not?
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们要用 Kubernetes 重写一切，因为为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And so we redo everything with
sentences.zh: 于是我们用

sentences.en: Kubernetes.
sentences.zh: Kubernetes 重做了一切。

sentences.en: And then like a year later, they're like, nah, let's move to AWS Lambda.
sentences.zh: 然后一年后，他们又说，不，让我们迁移到 AWS Lambda。

sentences.en: That's even cooler now.
sentences.zh: 那个现在更酷。

sentences.en: And it'll look better on our resume.
sentences.zh: 而且在简历上看起来更好看。

sentences.en: So then it's like, let's just spend the next, no, we're literally not going to ship a new feature.
sentences.zh: 所以就变成了，让我们花接下来的时间，不，我们实际上不会发布任何新功能。

sentences.en: We're too busy.
sentences.zh: 我们太忙了。

sentences.en: We're moving everything to
sentences.zh: 我们正在把一切迁移到

sentences.en: Kubernetes and Lambda, right?
sentences.zh: Kubernetes 和 Lambda，对吧？

sentences.en: Like that's what like people do this.
sentences.zh: 人们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And then they never deliver new functionality to their customers.
sentences.zh: 然后他们永远无法向客户交付新功能。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: Like I could go on this topic for like an hour.
sentences.zh: 我可以在这个话题上聊上一个小时。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I know I have a friend who works in the games industry and he says, you know, they go, I asked them really to describe what the, this crunch phenomenon was.
sentences.zh: 我知道有个朋友在游戏行业工作，他说，你知道，我问他能不能描述一下所谓的“加班潮”现象。

sentences.en: This was around the time when, um, you know, there was a lot of publicity around the crunch hours that game developers work and things like that.
sentences.zh: 那是在，嗯，你知道，关于游戏开发者加班时间等问题有很多舆论的时候。

sentences.en: Um, and you know, he basically explained to me really well, he said, it's, it's basically feature creep except, you know, because a game is kind of this atomic thing where you just
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他基本上向我解释得很清楚，他说，这基本上就是功能蔓延，只不过，你知道，因为游戏是一种原子化的东西，你只是

sentences.en: released the game.
sentences.zh: 发布了游戏。

sentences.en: Um, it's all hypothetical, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这都是假设，对吧？

sentences.en: So the, the, uh, uh, you know, the, the game designer will come to the engineers and say, Oh, we need to, uh, you know, add a, a 14th lineman in
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，你知道，游戏设计师会找到工程师说，哦，我们需要，呃，你知道，在

sentences.en: Madden.
sentences.zh: 《Madden》中增加第 14 个边锋。

sentences.en: Otherwise like no one will play this game.
sentences.zh: 否则没人会玩这个游戏。

sentences.en: And then they go and they like code it up and it's like, Oh, now the football needs to be orange.
sentences.zh: 然后他们去写代码，接着又说，哦，现在橄榄球需要变成橙色的。

sentences.en: It has to be orange.
sentences.zh: 它必须是橙色的。

sentences.en: Everyone loves orange.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢橙色。

sentences.en: And then,
sentences.zh: 然后，

sentences.en: Oh, now we want the person to be able to set the color.
sentences.zh: 哦，现在我们想让用户能够设置颜色。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so you get all of these changing requirements and, uh, and you're working these insane hours.
sentences.zh: 所以你得到了所有这些不断变化的需求，呃，你得疯狂加班。

sentences.en: And so then, you know, that's, that's one of the reasons why I think code quality on games has always been a challenge.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为这就是为什么游戏的代码质量一直是个挑战的原因之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Feature creep is a never ending problem in software development just, and, and to some sense developers are our own worst enemy on it too.
sentences.zh: 功能蔓延是软件开发中一个永无止境的问题，在某种意义上，开发者自己也是最大的敌人。

sentences.en: We're, you know, I'm talking to one of my team members this week and we use like a SQL parser that parses SQL statements and we're having problems with it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这周我和团队成员交谈，我们使用了一个解析 SQL 语句的 SQL 解析器，但我们遇到了问题。

sentences.en: And I'm like, okay, well if, and we use like a third party product to do this, we're like,
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，如果我们使用第三方产品来做这个，我们说，

sentences.en: okay, well, if it doesn't work, we have some fallback logic and we'll just, we'll just have this really little regular expressions that are fallback logic.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果它不工作，我们有一些回退逻辑，我们只要写一些很小的正则表达式作为回退逻辑就行了。

sentences.en: But my developer's like, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 但我的开发者说，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: We need to write our own SQL parser.
sentences.zh: 我们需要写我们自己的 SQL 解析器。

sentences.en: And I'm like, no, we don't, no, we really don't need to do that.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，我们不需要，我们真的不需要那样做。

sentences.en: We have other stuff to do, but that's what developers do, right?
sentences.zh: 我们还有别的事要做，但开发者就是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, well, people love building stuff.
sentences.zh: 人们就是喜欢造东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's where our own worst enemy of, you know, what I always say, like doing software development sideways, like we're not moving forward to like really improve our product
sentences.zh: 这就是我们自己最大的敌人，你知道，我常说，就像在软件开发中横向移动，我们没有向前推进以真正改进我们的产品

sentences.en: and deliver new stuff to our customers.
sentences.zh: 并向客户交付新东西。

sentences.en: We're just like moving sideways.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在横向移动。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You know, I wanted to piggyback on that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想顺着这个话题说一下。

sentences.en: So you make a product for developers, you know, when you started Stackify, were you afraid of that?
sentences.zh: 你为开发者制作产品，你知道，当你创办 Stackify 时，你害怕过这一点吗？

sentences.en: Cause that's one thing that I've always wondered.
sentences.zh: 因为这是我一直好奇的一件事。

sentences.en: And when we talked to a lot of folks who make, you know, who, for whom developers are the end user and, and, and, you
sentences.zh: 当我们和许多为开发者制作产品的人交谈时，你知道，开发者是最终用户，呃，其中一个恐惧就是你可以提供 99% 的功能，然后开发者说，不，我想为我自己的公司构建我自己的 Stackify。

sentences.en: know, one of the fears is that you can provide 99% of the functionality and then the developer says, no, I want to, I want to build my own Stackify for my own company.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何防范这种情况的呢？

sentences.en: And so how do you defend yourself against that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某个时间点，你真的无能为力。

sentences.en: I mean, there's really nothing you can do at some point in time.
sentences.zh: 你只能说不。

sentences.en: You just have to say no.
sentences.zh: 而且我们，你知道，这实际上是我必须时刻提醒我们团队的事情。

sentences.en: And we, you know, this is actually something I have to remind our teams all the time.
sentences.zh: 比如我们的客户会来找我们说，哦，Stackify 在这种“紫松鼠模式”下无法工作。

sentences.en: Like our customers will come to us and like, Oh, Stackify doesn't work in this like purple squirrel mode.
sentences.zh: 我们说，不，抱歉。

sentences.en: And we're like, Nope, sorry.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 它确实不支持。
